cards.back: It is home to a significant number of indigenous people, who have built homes around the reef's rich ecosystems for over 60,000 years.
Over 2 million people visit every year, it contributes around $6 billion a year, and about 64,000 people have jobs linked to the reef.
It is very biodiverse, with over 1,500 species of fish and 450 species of coral.
The crown-of-thorns starfish feeds on the coral, leaving it pale white and killing it, so creatures living there lose their home. Also coral bleaching.
Pollution from land-based run-off causes algal blooms, which boost the food supply for the crown-of-thorns starfish.

cards.front: When was the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority established?
cards.back: 1975 (it has zones with different levels of protection to conserve the reef)

cards.front: Great Barrier Reef: how does the tourism industry help preserve the reef?
cards.back: Boats are only allowed to dock in certain areas.
Coral seeding: moving bleached coral to help it recover.

questions.question: How long is the Great Barrier Reef?
questions.explanation: It is about 2,300 km long, made of 2,900 reefs and 900 islands.

questions.question: Which animal is a major natural threat to the Great Barrier Reef?
questions.explanation: The crown-of-thorns starfish feeds on coral, leaving it white and killing it.

questions.question: How many people visit the reef each year?
questions.explanation: Over 2 million visitors a year; about 64,000 people have jobs linked to the reef.

questions.question: How does pollution from land-based run-off harm the reef?
options: It causes algal blooms that feed crown-of-thorns starfish
questions.explanation: Run-off causes algal blooms, giving crown-of-thorns starfish more food so their numbers grow.

questions.question: In which year was the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority set up?
questions.explanation: It was established in 1975 and uses zones with different levels of protection.
